title: Keycloak lab: identity, OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect
summary: Two Ubuntu guests on keycloak-lan: Keycloak 26.4.7 with PostgreSQL and a Python app using Authorization Code + S256 PKCE. Seven exercises teach installation, realms, clients, users, roles, discovery, JWT validation, sessions and single sign-out, service credentials, refresh and real protocol failures. Example credentials only; deliberately HTTP for local learning.

exercises.title: Install and inspect Keycloak
exercises.text: Read the installation recipe: pinned official archive and SHA-256, Java 21, PostgreSQL and a systemd unit. This isolated lab deliberately uses start-dev and HTTP; the guides explain production hostname and TLS.

commands: sudo -u postgres psql -d keycloak -c 'SELECT name FROM realm;'

exercises.title: Realm, clients, users and roles
exercises.text: Use the console to create practice-console, a public client, learner and reader; repeat through kcadm in practice-cli. The independent lab realm remains the known test fixture. kc-lab wraps the real kcadm.sh with a temporary authenticated config.

commands: kc-lab create clients -r practice-cli -s clientId=practice-web -s publicClient=true -s standardFlowEnabled=true
kc-lab create users -r practice-cli -s username=learner -s enabled=true
kc-lab delete realms/practice-cli    # clean up only this practice realm

exercises.title: OIDC discovery, JWKS and claims
exercises.text: Discovery advertises endpoints; JWKS supplies public signing keys. Decode a token to read it, but only signature, issuer, audience and expiry verification can authorize a request.

commands: xdg-open http://127.0.0.1:18081/tokens    # verified access and ID claims

exercises.title: Authorization Code + PKCE and single sign-out
exercises.text: The browser receives a code, the app exchanges it with its private verifier. Tokens stay in the app; its cookie carries only an opaque session ID. Login twice in the same browser to create two app sessions under one Keycloak SSO session; logout invalidates both.

commands: xdg-open http://127.0.0.1:18081/    # Login, Protected, Read token claims, Refresh / logout
vmctl group test keycloak-lab    # includes the complete HTML form flow and SSO logout

exercises.title: Roles become application authorization
exercises.text: Alice has editor and /edit returns 200. Bob can authenticate but has no editor role, so /edit returns 403. A role change affects newly minted tokens; existing signed access tokens keep their claims until refresh/expiry.

commands: xdg-open http://127.0.0.1:18081/edit    # try Alice, logout, then Bob
kc-lab remove-roles -r lab --uusername alice --rolename editor    # new Alice login now gets 403
kc-lab add-roles -r lab --uusername alice --rolename editor    # restore before tests

exercises.title: Service tokens, refresh, expiry and introspection
exercises.text: Client credentials authenticates a service, not Alice. The service token lasts five seconds, carries lab-api as audience and has no refresh token. User tokens last 120 seconds and refresh tokens rotate; reuse is rejected.

commands: xdg-open http://127.0.0.1:18081/actions    # log in first, refresh the user token

exercises.title: Read protocol errors
exercises.text: Observe exact status codes and errors: invalid redirect 400, wrong secret 401 unauthorized_client, wrong verifier/reused code 400 invalid_grant, expired or tampered bearer 401. Tests also reject unsolicited callbacks and forged CSRF.
